description: We are students and professionals in different fields. Programming, physics and robotics are our main fields.
summary: Have you ever wondered what Mars really looks like, or how we learned what we know about it? Get ready for take-off and join Opportunity on Mars. You drive the rover through its real 14-year journey, from its landing in 2004 to its last message in 2018, and discover its difficulties and discoveries by doing, not by reading. Opportunity is still sitting silently in Perseverance Valley today: Smell of Rust brings this abandoned explorer back to life.
details:
Smell of Rust's project solution

Smell of Rust is an educational 3D game about the rovers humanity has left on Mars. Players drive the rover themselves and complete short missions based on its real discoveries, using its real instruments: the Pancam, the robotic arm with the Microscopic Imager, the Rock Abrasion Tool (RAT), the APXS and the Mössbauer spectrometer. This first version focuses on Opportunity.

Along the way, players also meet the hardware Opportunity left behind: its lander in Eagle Crater and the debris of its own heat shield, next to which it found the first meteorite ever identified on another planet. The story ends where the real rover rests today.

Between missions, a map built from NASA HiRISE images shows the rover’s real route and distance, and the number of sols and Earth years that passed. Each discovery is added to a scientific notebook, where players can compare the game with the real NASA photos.
Link to our gitlab: https://gitlab.com/MaverickMessier/nasal_space_challenge

A clock and a map are displayed on the screen which enables players to orient themselves in time and space as they follow Opportunity in his journey.

Nine missions were implemented in the game. Each time a mission is accomplished, the player will be able to follow his progress and what they have discovered in the scientific notebook of the game.

Let's have a look at the different quests :

1.Landing in Eagle Crater (Sol 1, January 2004) —Take the first Pancam panorama, drive off the lander, reach the rocky outcrop. Introduces the rover and the sedimentary rocks that proved liquid water once existed at Meridiani Planum.

2.The blueberries and El Capitan (Sol 36) — Approach the hematite “blueberries,” deploy the arm, image them with the Microscopic Imager, then grind El Capitan with the RAT and analyse it with APXS and Mössbauer. The spherules formed in water — the mission's first major discovery.

3.Endurance Crater (Sol 133) — enter at Karatepe, grind and analyse a layer, reach Burns Cliff, climb back out. A deep look at Martian stratigraphy.

4.Heat Shield Rock: a meteorite! (Sol 339) — Drive to the heat-shield debris, photograph it, then identify the dark rock with Mössbauer and APXS. It became the first meteorite ever identified on another planet.

5.Stuck in Purgatory Dune (Sol 446)— Cross a sand ripple, get bogged down, and reverse out slowly. A gameplay lesson based on the real five-week extraction that taught engineers how to drive on Mars sand.

6.Erebus Crater (Sol 633) — Study of the Olympia and Payson outcrops around an ancient crater that has been almost entirely eroded away. Grind Kalavrita with the RAT and then take a photographs with the Microscopic Image.

7.Victoria Crater (Sol 951) — Reach Duck Bay at the crater rim (watch the cliff), photograph Cape Verde, and take a grand panorama. The layered cliffs recorded hundreds of thousands of years of Martian history.

8.Homestake: a vein of gypsum (Sol 2765) — Approach the pale vein, image it with the Microscopic Imager, and analyse its chemistry with APXS. Gypsum means water once flowed through fractures at the rim of Endeavour Crater.

9.The 2018 dust storm (Sol 5111) — Photograph Perseverance Valley, watch the storm arrive, send one last message to Earth, and put the rover into hibernation. The mission's ending, based on the real loss of contact on 10 June 2018.

The game benefits

anyone curious and enthusiastic about space exploration, planetary science by:

  • Educating players on the Mars exploration mission and more specifically about the Opportunity rover.
  • Remembering the previous rovers that contributed to improve our knowledge about Mars and the legacy that will continue after it.
  • Bridging the gap between NASA’s informations and the general public.

Our goal

NASA’s informations about Mars rovers is rich but spread across many technical pages. Smell of Rust brings it together in an experience that feels like exploring, not like homework, especially for school-age players. We aim for accuracy: dates, distances, instruments and telemetry come from NASA and JPL sources. Some elements, such as driving speed and the atmosphere, are simplified for gameplay. The game is bilingual (English and French) and was designed to grow to other rovers: Spirit, Curiosity, Perseverance and Ingenuity.

Tools and Technologies Used

Coding Languages:

  • C#
  • Unity→ for 3D game development.
  • FLStudio→ for the music and the sound effects
  • Gitlab

Data Sources:

  • We mainly used the information and pictures provided by NASA websites. To complete the resources we also looked at scientific paper as well as the mars exploration rover telecommunications guide.
  • NASA/JPL/University of Arizona HiRISE elevation data (terrain).
  • NASA 3D models of Mars and of the Mars Exploration Rover.
  • NASA/JPL Photojournal images (in the notebook).
  • NASA/JPL mission updates and press releases (dates, odometry, final telemetry).
  • The Mars Exploration Rover telecommunications guide.
  • Published papers on the Meridiani outcrops.
